title: S-shaped income dynamics: poverty trap evidence is mixed
body:
The Banerjee–Duflo critique of strict poverty trap models pushed back on Sachs-style 'big push' arguments.
[Step] Survey
  [Input] Banerjee & Duflo 2011, Kraay & McKenzie 2014, Balboni et al. 2022 Bangladesh asset transfers
[Step] Observation
  [Output] strict S-shaped income dynamics show up in some asset-transfer experiments (Balboni et al.) but not in cross-country growth data
[Step] Interpretation
  [Output] poverty traps may exist at the household-asset level without being visible at the country level
The two literatures are arguing about different objects. Reconciliation may not be a single yes/no answer about traps but a question of which assets, at which scale, exhibit non-convex returns. I am not confident enough in this to treat it as settled.
